featured_reviews.name: Samruddhi Rane
featured_reviews.review_text:
Saheli Working Women Hostel has a very poor system. First of all, false information is given to girls. In the agreement, it is mentioned that the bed charge is ₹3000 and food charge is ₹3000, but when a girl decides to stay only for accommodation, they ask for ₹4000 or ₹5000, even though the food charge is only ₹1000 less.

Secondly, the food quality is not good at all, and girls are often scolded regarding food issues. The cook even orders girls to make chapatis themselves. If the current month rent is not paid on time, food service is stopped, which is completely wrong.

On my floor, some girls were even sleeping in the hall because there were no fans in the rooms, yet full fees were still charged. Also, every girl is charged different bed fees, which is an unfair system.

They even ask the girls to clean the toilet and washroom floors themselves. We have to wash our own utensils and do almost everything on our own, yet they charge ₹6000 and now suddenly increased it to ₹7000. Even the food quality is not good.

Apart from this, there have been no safety issues, but the management system is very poor and unfair.

featured_reviews.name: tejal sawant
featured_reviews.review_text: Saheli is a hostel that feels like home. As the name suggests, there are excellent food facilities here, as well as cleanliness and neatness. The atmosphere here, the girls who cooperate with each other from time to time, as well as the director of the institution who stands by us in every problem, spacious rooms, and entertainment facilities are all very nice. The staff here also treats us like family members; while staying here, it does not feel like we are living in a hostel; we constantly feel like we are living in a happy environment like home. Saheli has fully thought of both the safety of the girls and the affordable living of the poor for only Rs. 3000.

featured_reviews.name: maya pawar
featured_reviews.review_text: I had a great stay at Saheli Ladies Hostel! The rooms were clean and comfortable, making it feel like home. The staff was friendly and always ready to help with anything I needed. The location is safe and close to shops and transport. I loved the community vibe with other ladies living there. Overall, it was an excellent experience, and I highly recommend it!

featured_reviews.name: Maya
featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the worst and most horrible experiences I have ever faced was choosing this dormitory. These people scam you, and let me tell you how. I booked this place for 7 days through Agoda, and it was around 1400 rupees plus. They gave me a dormitory bed with AC, but an hour later they claimed I had booked non-AC. When I requested a non-AC bed instead, they said those were only for men. They only turned on the AC at night. They demanded an extra 700 rupees, but I immediately contacted Agoda, and they confirmed I didn't need to pay any additional amount. They even sent an email to the dormitory about it. If you've booked this place through Agoda, please don't pay a single extra penny to this unscrupulous dormitory.

The second issue was bed bugs. I was in Mumbai for work and had an important day the next day after checking in. I couldn't sleep because of bed bugs on the upper bunk beds, and they didn't change the bed sheets or pillow covers. I changed beds three times, but it didn't solve the problem. Eventually, I couldn't take it anymore and complained to the assistant manager. His response was, "So what should I do now?" Are you kidding me? It's your damn dormitory; just clean it every time someone checks out. I couldn't sleep the whole day. I had booked for 7 days, but I asked for a refund. Initially, he refused, offering to arrange a bed instead, which I rejected. Eventually, he charged me 300 rupees for a day, but when I booked through Agoda, it was only around 187 rupees. I had a horrible experience with these people.

featured_reviews.review_text:

To average in this area, considering them low price, the conditions ate quite good. Toilet and showers are functional and clean. Space inside is very narrow, especially on second floor, where beds are set in 3 levels, which is too much, and drives a fire safety violation.
Around the place, in 2 minutes walk there are drugstore, groceries, and local canteen. District itself is dirty and overcrowded, with no places of interest and parks around. So hostel is suitable generally for 1-2 nights stay no longer.

featured_reviews.name: Rafiya farheen
featured_reviews.review_text:
I took this PG for one month, but unfortunately I had to leave within just 3 days due to serious issues.
Firstly, the PG is not organized or properly managed by the owner, Mansi. There is no hygiene maintained. The washroom and washbasin are extremely dirty and unclean. The kitchen is not properly accessible — only a few people are allowed to use it, while others are restricted. You cannot cook properly.
This is the month of Ramzan, and when I raised concerns regarding basic facilities, my complaints were ignored. The warden clearly refused washing clothes saying, “If I get time, I will do,” which is very unprofessional. There is also theft happening — many residents’ belongings are going missing.
Most importantly, there is no proper space or freedom to offer namaz peacefully. When I complained about these issues, the warden behaved rudely and misbehaved. After the owner Mansi leaves, arguments continue till 2 AM, disturbing everyone and that cause me a mental Harrasement.
The warden is a 19-year-old girl from Nepal who does not understand our language properly and is not capable of managing the PG responsibly.
There is a prepaid system — if you pay for one full month, there is strictly no refund under any circumstances. Even though the facilities and commitments promised on the first day were not fulfilled, they refused to consider any refund.
Because of all this, I lost my full amount of ₹6,000 within just 3 days.
Overall, it was a very stressful and disappointing experience. Basic hygiene, proper management, safety, and respect for residents are completely lacking.

The Kurla PG offers good facilities and overall management, but there is a serious issue with the warden’s behavior. She shows clear favoritism towards a few girls (such as Rehna and Mohana) by doing their personal work and letting them control the lights, while treating others unfairly.
Additionally, late-night disturbances are common, with some residents talking on calls till 3 AM, making it difficult to study or sleep peacefully.

featured_reviews.name: Janki Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have stayed in this hostel for one year. The owner Sangeeta Aunty and Sanjay Uncle are abit strict but cooperative.

Firstly, the location is very commutable. They have a bus stop right next to the main hostel gate. It is located on a busy road and auto is also available easily.

Secondly, the hostel is not that spacious but its clean and safe. They have installed cameras all over the place and security is also maintained at the entry gate. Every room has storage space, bunk beds, a TV and table chairs. The washrooms and bathroom are kept very clean and hygienic. They have a microwave, fridge and washing machine in common on all floors.

Thirdly, the rent. It is expensive as compared to other places but the amenities and location justifies its rent.
